Definition: diminutive of στρουθός (a sparrow); a little sparrow:--sparrow.
BiblicalUsage: The little sparrow is the cheapest bird in the market, and the most remembered. Two sparrows are sold for a farthing, and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father, and the hairs of your head are all numbered: fear not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sparrow is the proof of the Father's care: He counts the cheap birds, and He counts your hairs.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
